messages:
Elena (Cust): Hey team, after we pinned our model to a reserved instance this morning, our embedding store client started failing with an assertion about vector shape. We send 1536-d vectors but the API is returning 1024-d responses.

sophie (support): Sorry you're hitting this, can you paste the request+response (sanitized) and the model id you pinned to?

Elena (Cust): Sure — we call POST /v1/embeddings with model
```json
{
  \"model\": \"openembed-large-v2:pinned-2026-03-17\",
  \"input\": [\"sample text\"]
}
```
Response body (truncated):
```json
{
  \"data\": [{
    \"embedding\": [0.0001, 0.0012, ...]  // length: 1024
  }],
  \"model\": \"openembed-large-v2:pinned-2026-03-17\"
}
```
Indexing client then asserts `expected_len == len(embedding)` and fails. This started precisely after the reserved capacity rollout at 09:12 UTC (we roll on a schedule).

jamal (infra): ops-bot shows a reserved-deploy event at 09:11:58 for that variant — tagging it: res-deploy-6731. cc @ryan (ml).

ops-bot: Deployment res-deploy-6731 completed on pool-dedicated-3 (gpu-a100x8) at 09:11:58 UTC — variant image: openembed-large-v2:2026-03-17-quant.

ryan (ml): Quick theory: looks like the pinned variant may have fallen back to a smaller quantized model artifact with a different output head (1024). Two things to check: model manifest (vector_size) and any automatic variant-substitution rules.

sophie (support): Elena, can you run a direct curl from your client to reproduce and include the full Content-Length and headers? also, do you have a cached embedding schema on your side?

Elena (Cust): Repro steps I ran locally:
1) curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED' -d '{\"model\":\"openembed-large-v2:pinned-2026-03-17\",\"input\":\"hello\"}'
2) Got response with embedding len 1024.
3) Rolling back the pin to previous variant restores 1536-d outputs immediately.

jamal (infra): Can confirm from service logs we saw a compatibility fallback for that reserved pool around 09:11:57 due to a kernel selection mismatch. The runtime substituted a quantized-compatible artifact: openembed-large-v2:quant-1024. That variant reports model.metadata.vector_size=1024.

ryan (ml): That explains it. The platform should have translated that substitution into the response model name, but looks like we returned the pinned model id while serving the quant artifact — mismatch between reported model id and actual embedding shape. Bug: serving/runtime not syncing reported model metadata when performing variant fallback for reserved pools.

sophie (support): Short term workaround: avoid pinning to that exact reserved artifact or pin to a variant that specifies vector_size 1024 explicitly so your indexer can adapt; longer term we need a fix so response includes accurate output dimension in model field or a `vector_shape` field in response.

Elena (Cust): We need a safe rollback plan — can you confirm whether unpinning will cause any downtime or throttling?

jamal (infra): Unpin relies on routing to hosted model pool; for your account it will switch to hosted instances with no downtime but may have transient rate limiting for a few seconds. We can do the unpin now and keep the older variant id pinned to your reserved pool until a fix is out.

ryan (ml): Action items I/O:
- [ ] Add server-side guard to ensure response.model reflects served artifact (ryan)
- [ ] Emit explicit `embedding_dimensions` in responses (api team)
- [ ] Add a tooling check to surface variant substitution events to customers (jamal)
- [ ] Support will coordinate rollback and confirm indexing compatibility with Elena (sophie)

sophie (support): Elena, I'll schedule the rollback in 10 minutes and monitor. Can you confirm indexer tolerates duplicate vectors for a few minutes?

Elena (Cust): Yes we can tolerate duplicates briefly. Please proceed. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: Rollback triggered for customer account cust-842 at 09:28:03 UTC by sophie. Rolling to variant openembed-large-v2:stable-1536.

jamal (infra): Follow-up: logs show successful serve from stable-1536 at 09:28:11 and embedding lengths returned to 1536.

Elena (Cust): Confirmed — indexing resumed and assertion errors stopped. Thank you.

sophie (support): Leaving this open until we have a fix. I'll post an update in ~48h. :eyes:

ryan (ml): I'll create the ticket for the runtime fix and the API change, link it here when ready.

Elena (Cust): Appreciate the quick turnaround.

--- end of thread
